fields.meta_description: Take a free supplement quiz that matches you to capsules, gummies, powders, or liquids. Then build one that sells from your own shelf.
fields.h1: Build a Supplement Quiz That Matches Shoppers to Your Products
fields.hero_description: Build a supplement quiz that matches shoppers to products by how they like to take them, or try the eight-question one below.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Supplement Quiz on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A supplement quiz sorts shoppers into the formats you stock. Emergent builds the questions, the results, and the table behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Results named after the formats you sell

List the formats on your shelf, such as capsules and gummies. Emergent writes the questions so that every option counts toward one of them, and you reword any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Your products on each result screen

Tag each product in the app's product table with the result it suits and a diet label, such as vegan. The result screen lists the tagged items, and a retag shows on the next quiz.
fields.feature_3:
Medicine questions handed to a person

Add a question about prescription medicines, and a Yes skips the product list. The app emails your pharmacist a link, and the answers stay in the database, out of the inbox.
fields.feature_4:
A conversational flow sized for a thumb

Emergent builds the quiz as a conversational flow with one question per screen. A shopper holding a phone in the store aisle can answer all eight and see a result before checkout.
fields.feature_5:
Every finished quiz kept as a row

Each result, the options picked, and an email when one is given save as one row in a database you own. Filter by Powders to see what time of day those shoppers take one.
fields.feature_6:
On your domain, with code you can keep

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the quiz can sit at your store's address. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Shops Running a Supplement Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
For a Gummies result, the vegan gummies come first

Sarafina Duvernay answers eight questions on Vesperline Nutrition's site and lands on Gummies. Her result screen lists the 3 vegan gummies the company tagged for that format, starting with its daily multivitamin. Her answers and email are stored in Vesperline's shopper table.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a shopper takes a prescription, the pharmacist steps in

Every quiz at the Copperwell Pharmacy counter asks whether the shopper takes a prescription medicine, since some supplements might interact with medicines. A Yes ends on "Ask our pharmacist" instead of a product list. Pharmacist Zuleika Amaro gets an email that says a quiz is in, with a link and no answers in it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Refill email at day 25 of a 30-day tub

Each subscriber at Saltmeadow Daily gets a 30-day supply in the format their quiz result named. Iduna Kincaid landed on Powders, so a tub ships to her each month. On day 25, the app emails her a refill reminder, 5 days before the tub runs out, with a link to skip a month or switch formats.
fields.tab_content_4:
In the fall, capsules led with 480 of 1,200

A tablet by the register at Bramblecrest Market runs the supplement quiz. This fall, 1,200 shoppers finished it: Capsules led with 480, then Gummies at 360, Powders at 220, and Liquids at 140. Owner Ferdinand Tavakoli doubled the capsule shelf.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a supplement quiz?

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a supplement quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 is supplement brands' own finders and health-library vitamin quizzes, and every one asks about health to name a product, which is advice a store quiz should not give. This page gives a visitor an eight-question supplement quiz they can take right here that matches them to a format (capsules, gummies, powders, or daily packs) by how they like to take one, never by symptoms, and then shows four businesses running their own: a vitamin brand showing the products it tagged for each result, a pharmacy that sends any prescription answer to the pharmacist, a subscription brand timing refill reminders, and a market restocking from result counts. Every answer stays in a database the owner keeps, and the FAQ covers wording, privacy, medication questions, and what a result screen should say.
tab_stories: Sarafina Duvernay answers eight questions on Vesperline Nutrition's site, lands on Gummies, and sees the 3 vegan gummies the company tagged for that format, with her answers stored in its shopper table.

Copperwell Pharmacy runs the quiz on a counter tablet, and a Yes to the prescription question ends on a screen that says to ask the pharmacist instead of a product list, while pharmacist Zuleika Amaro gets an email that a quiz is in with a link and no answers in it.
Saltmeadow Daily ships a 30-day supply in the format each result names, and the app emails Iduna Kincaid a refill reminder 5 days before her Powders tub runs out.
Bramblecrest Market keeps the quiz on a tablet by the register, 1,200 shoppers finish it in the fall with Capsules leading at 480, and owner Ferdinand Tavakoli doubles the capsule shelf.
